newsitem.title: LATVIA: INTERVIEW-LATVIA BOURSE NEEDS MORE LISTINGS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-LATVIA BOURSE NEEDS MORE LISTINGS.

text.p: The Latvian bourse needs some five to eight new listings in 1997 to create more stability on the market, an official of the planned securities market commission, said on Thursday.

"It would be ideal if we managed to have some five to eight new companies, not the ones being privatised. That would create more stability," Talis Laizans, the future deputy chairman of the commission told Reuters.
Laizans currently works as head of treasury at the Latvian Investment Bank but has already been confirmed as deputy head of the commission, which is still under formation.
Laizans said the market had a big speculative element which could be evened out by new listings.

Laizans said existing equities laws provided a good working environment but some issues, like issues of prospectuses and information to be provided to the public needed to be brought to a higher level.
"We have to more clearly define the process and methodology of providing public company information," Laizans said.
There was a need for Latvian equities legislation to be harmonised with EU legislation, he added.
The seucirites commission, a state regulatory body, is expected to start full-scale activities later this month, when parliament confirms the line-up of its board.
